turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: Alright everyone, thanks for joining. Today we need to plan the Aurora launch event end to end, so let's go through each workstream and leave with clear owners and deadlines.

turns.speaker: Alice
turns.text: Sounds good. I think we should start with the venue, because everything else depends on the date and the location.

turns.speaker: Claire
turns.text: Agreed. Before we dive in, can we confirm the event date so everyone is working toward the same target?

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: Yes, the launch event is set for May 20. That gives us about two months to get everything ready.

turns.speaker: Emma
turns.text: Two months is tight but doable. Let's make sure we book the big things first so we don't lose availability.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: I'll keep a shared checklist so we can track what is decided and what is still open across all the workstreams.

turns.speaker: Hugo
turns.text: Perfect. Let's also remember to keep every decision in this chat so nothing gets lost between meetings.

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: Great, let's begin. Alice, the venue is yours first.

turns.speaker: Alice
turns.text: I'll take responsibility for the venue, since I've already visited a few places around the city.

turns.speaker: Alice
turns.text: We need a space that can comfortably hold around three hundred people and that is easy to reach by public transport.

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: Make sure it has proper wheelchair access too, because that is a hard requirement for us this year.

turns.speaker: Alice
turns.text: Good point, I'll add that to the list. It also needs a separate room where we can run the hands-on workshops.

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: By the way, when do we actually need to have the venue confirmed and signed?

turns.speaker: Alice
turns.text: We have to lock in the venue by March 15, otherwise we lose the early-bird rate and the date might slip.

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: And how much can we spend on the venue in total?

turns.speaker: Alice
turns.text: The budget for the venue is twelve thousand euros, and that amount has to cover the deposit as well.

turns.speaker: Alice
turns.text: I've narrowed it down to two options. GrandHall is central, spacious, and already has most of the equipment we need.

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: What about the Riverside Center? It is noticeably cheaper, but it is quite far from the train station.

turns.speaker: Alice
turns.text: Riverside is cheaper, but with three hundred guests arriving, the transport problem is a real dealbreaker.

turns.speaker: Alice
turns.text: So let's go with GrandHall for the venue. I'll start the paperwork and confirm the date with them.

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: Who do we talk to at GrandHall to get the contract moving?

turns.speaker: Alice
turns.text: Our contact at GrandHall is Marie Lambert, she is the events manager and she handles all the bookings.

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: Can you share her number so I can call her about the deposit this afternoon?

turns.speaker: Alice
turns.text: Sure, you can reach Marie Lambert at +33 6 12 34 56 01, she usually answers quickly.

turns.speaker: Alice
turns.text: I'll email her the full requirements today and copy everyone here so we are all aligned.

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: Perfect, thanks for taking this on, it is one less thing for the rest of us to worry about.

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: I'll handle the catering, I've worked with a couple of good providers on previous events.

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: We need food for three hundred people, with clear vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free options labeled on every dish.

turns.speaker: Emma
turns.text: Please also account for allergies, we had a serious nut allergy issue at the last event and we cannot repeat that.

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: Absolutely, I'll require a full allergen chart from whoever we pick, and separate preparation for the free-from meals.

turns.speaker: Emma
turns.text: When do we need to give the caterer the final headcount and menu?

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: The caterer needs the final numbers by March 20, so I'll collect dietary requirements from the registration team before then.

turns.speaker: Emma
turns.text: What budget are we working with for the food and service?

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: We have eight thousand five hundred euros for catering, which works out to roughly twenty-eight euros per person.

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: I'm considering FreshTable, they do seasonal menus and they were very reliable when we used them last spring.

turns.speaker: Emma
turns.text: There is also BistroEvent, they are a bit cheaper but I'm not sure they can handle three hundred covers smoothly.

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: Right, scaling to three hundred is exactly where the cheaper option gets risky, so reliability matters more here.

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: Let's choose FreshTable for the catering, I'll send them the brief and the allergen requirements.

turns.speaker: Emma
turns.text: Who is the person we coordinate with at FreshTable?

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: Our contact at FreshTable is Julien Roy, he is the head chef and he manages the event menus directly.

turns.speaker: Emma
turns.text: Could you pass me his number? I want to confirm the vegan options with him.

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: Of course, you can reach Julien Roy at +33 6 12 34 56 02, he prefers calls in the morning.

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: I'll set up a tasting session next week and invite a few of us to validate the menu before we sign.

turns.speaker: Emma
turns.text: Great idea, a tasting will catch any problems early, thanks Bruno.

turns.speaker: Claire
turns.text: I'll own the event website and the online marketing, since I've been building our landing pages all year.

turns.speaker: Claire
turns.text: The site needs a clear agenda, speaker bios, a registration button, and it must work perfectly on mobile phones.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: It should also load fast, people will open it from the invitation email and we lose them if it is slow.

turns.speaker: Claire
turns.text: Agreed, I'll keep the pages lightweight and add a simple FAQ so we get fewer support emails before the event.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: When does the website need to be live and tested?

turns.speaker: Claire
turns.text: The website has to be live by April 2, so we can start driving registrations a full month before the event.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: How much have we set aside for the website work?

turns.speaker: Claire
turns.text: The budget for the website is six thousand euros, covering design, development, and the hosting for the year.

turns.speaker: Claire
turns.text: I'm talking to WebNova, they specialize in event sites and can deliver a polished result quickly.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Could we just use our existing template instead? It would save money, though it is less flexible.

turns.speaker: Claire
turns.text: The template saves money but it cannot handle the registration flow we need, so a custom build is worth it here.

turns.speaker: Claire
turns.text: Let's go with WebNova for the website, I'll share the wireframes and the content plan with them.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Who is our point of contact at WebNova?

turns.speaker: Claire
turns.text: Our contact at WebNova is Sofia Martin, she is the project lead and she will run the whole build.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Can I get her number to coordinate the hosting setup?

turns.speaker: Claire
turns.text: Yes, you can reach Sofia Martin at +33 6 12 34 56 03, she is very responsive on technical questions.

turns.speaker: Claire
turns.text: I'll draft all the page copy this week so the developers are never waiting on content.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Nice, keeping content ahead of development is exactly how we avoid a last-minute rush.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: I'll take care of the audio and video, I want the keynote to look and sound professional for everyone in the room.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: We need a reliable sound system, two large screens, and a recording setup so we can publish the talks afterwards.

turns.speaker: Alice
turns.text: Please make sure the microphones are wireless and that we have spares, last year one died mid-talk.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Good call, I'll budget for backup microphones and a dedicated technician who stays in the room the whole time.

turns.speaker: Alice
turns.text: When do we need to confirm the AV equipment and the technician?

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: We need to confirm the AV setup by March 28, because the good technicians get booked up fast in spring.

turns.speaker: Alice
turns.text: What is the budget for audio and video?

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: The AV budget is nine thousand five hundred euros, which includes the recording and the on-site technician.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: SoundPro is my first choice, they handled a similar conference for us and the sound was flawless.

turns.speaker: Alice
turns.text: What about VisualEvent? They quote lower, but I haven't seen their work on a room this size.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: VisualEvent is cheaper but unproven at this scale, and bad sound would ruin the keynote, so I'd rather not risk it.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Let's book SoundPro for the audio and video, I'll send them the room layout and the technical needs.

turns.speaker: Alice
turns.text: Who do we coordinate with at SoundPro?

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Our contact at SoundPro is Lucas Bernard, he is the technical director and he will oversee the installation.

turns.speaker: Alice
turns.text: Can you share his number so I can ask about the screen dimensions?

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Sure, you can reach Lucas Bernard at +33 6 12 34 56 04, he knows the venue already.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: I'll schedule a site visit with them so they can test the acoustics before the event day.

turns.speaker: Alice
turns.text: That site visit is a good safety net, thanks for being thorough David.

turns.speaker: Emma
turns.text: I'll manage registration and ticketing, I want the sign-up process to be smooth from the first click to the confirmation email.

turns.speaker: Emma
turns.text: We need a system that handles three hundred registrations, sends confirmations, and lets us track dietary requirements.

turns.speaker: Hugo
turns.text: It should also support a waitlist, because if we hit capacity we don't want to just turn people away.

turns.speaker: Emma
turns.text: Yes, a waitlist plus automatic notifications when a spot opens up, that keeps interested people engaged.

turns.speaker: Hugo
turns.text: When does the registration system need to be ready to accept sign-ups?

turns.speaker: Emma
turns.text: Registration has to open by April 10, right after the website goes live, so the two need to be connected.

turns.speaker: Hugo
turns.text: What budget do we have for the ticketing platform?

turns.speaker: Emma
turns.text: The registration budget is three thousand euros, mostly platform fees and the payment processing costs.

turns.speaker: Emma
turns.text: TicketFlow looks ideal, it has built-in waitlists and it integrates easily with the website.

turns.speaker: Hugo
turns.text: There is also EventBrite, everyone knows it, but their fees per ticket add up at our scale.

turns.speaker: Emma
turns.text: EventBrite is familiar but the per-ticket fees would eat our budget, so TicketFlow is the better fit financially.

turns.speaker: Emma
turns.text: Let's use TicketFlow for registration, I'll configure the forms and connect it to the website.

turns.speaker: Hugo
turns.text: Who is our contact at TicketFlow?

turns.speaker: Emma
turns.text: Our contact at TicketFlow is Nina Petit, she is the account manager and she helps with the setup.

turns.speaker: Hugo
turns.text: Can I have her number to ask about the payment integration?

turns.speaker: Emma
turns.text: Yes, you can reach Nina Petit at +33 6 12 34 56 05, she handles all the technical onboarding.

turns.speaker: Emma
turns.text: I'll run a test registration end to end this week to make sure the confirmation emails actually arrive.

turns.speaker: Hugo
turns.text: Testing the whole flow early is smart, thanks Emma.

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: Quick pause before we continue. Now that the venue and the date are fixed, let's make sure every workstream is aligned on May 20.

turns.speaker: Claire
turns.text: The website and registration both depend on that date, so I'll hard-code May 20 everywhere to avoid any confusion.

turns.speaker: Emma
turns.text: I'll also add the date to every confirmation email, because people always ask even when it is on the site.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: One thing across all workstreams: we should keep a single shared contact sheet so anyone can reach any vendor quickly.

turns.speaker: Alice
turns.text: Good idea David, I'll start that sheet with the venue contact and everyone can add their own vendor as we go.

turns.speaker: Hugo
turns.text: Let's also agree on a contingency plan, if a vendor falls through we need to know who decides and how fast.

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: If any vendor falls through, the workstream owner decides the replacement and flags it here within twenty-four hours.

turns.speaker: Emma
turns.text: That clear rule helps a lot, let's keep going with the remaining workstreams.

turns.speaker: Hugo
turns.text: I'll lead sponsorship, my goal is to bring in partners who cover part of the cost and add credibility to the event.

turns.speaker: Hugo
turns.text: We need a sponsorship deck with clear tiers, and a list of companies whose audience matches ours.

turns.speaker: Claire
turns.text: Make sure the tiers offer real visibility, sponsors want their logo on the site and a mention during the keynote.

turns.speaker: Hugo
turns.text: Exactly, I'll define gold, silver, and bronze tiers with logo placement, a booth, and speaking slots as the benefits.

turns.speaker: Claire
turns.text: When do we need to have the sponsorship agreements signed?

turns.speaker: Hugo
turns.text: We need the sponsorship deals signed by April 5, so we can print the logos and announce the partners in time.

turns.speaker: Claire
turns.text: How much sponsorship revenue are we targeting?

turns.speaker: Hugo
turns.text: We are targeting twenty thousand euros in sponsorship, which would cover a big part of the venue and catering costs.

turns.speaker: Hugo
turns.text: BrandLink is my top prospect, they sponsor similar tech events and their audience is exactly who we want to reach.

turns.speaker: Claire
turns.text: There is also PartnerPlus, but they tend to ask for a lot of control over the content in exchange.

turns.speaker: Hugo
turns.text: PartnerPlus gives money but wants editorial control, and that is not a trade I want to make for this launch.

turns.speaker: Hugo
turns.text: Let's pursue BrandLink for sponsorship, I'll send them the deck and propose a gold tier partnership.

turns.speaker: Claire
turns.text: Who is the person we negotiate with at BrandLink?

turns.speaker: Hugo
turns.text: Our contact at BrandLink is Omar Diallo, he is the partnerships director and he makes the funding decisions.

turns.speaker: Claire
turns.text: Can you share his number so I can loop him into the branding discussion?

turns.speaker: Hugo
turns.text: Sure, you can reach Omar Diallo at +33 6 12 34 56 06, he is expecting our proposal this week.

turns.speaker: Hugo
turns.text: I'll follow up with a call two days after sending the deck, that usually keeps the conversation moving.

turns.speaker: Claire
turns.text: Good plan, a timely follow-up makes a big difference with sponsors, thanks Hugo.

turns.speaker: Alice
turns.text: I'll also handle the keynote speakers, since I've been in touch with a few interesting people in the industry.

turns.speaker: Alice
turns.text: We want one strong opening keynote and two shorter talks, all focused on the future of smart home technology.

turns.speaker: Emma
turns.text: Please confirm the speakers early, attendees often decide to come based on who is speaking.

turns.speaker: Alice
turns.text: Agreed, the speaker lineup is a big part of our marketing, so I'll lock the names before we launch the site.

turns.speaker: Emma
turns.text: When do we need the keynote speakers confirmed?

turns.speaker: Alice
turns.text: We need the keynote speakers confirmed by March 25, so Claire can publish their bios when the site goes live.

turns.speaker: Emma
turns.text: What budget do we have for the speakers?

turns.speaker: Alice
turns.text: The speaker budget is seven thousand euros, covering fees and travel for the three talks.

turns.speaker: Alice
turns.text: SpeakerHub is a great option, they represent experienced speakers and handle all the logistics for us.

turns.speaker: Emma
turns.text: Could we invite someone directly instead? It might be cheaper, but it is more work to manage.

turns.speaker: Alice
turns.text: Going direct is cheaper but riskier on reliability, and SpeakerHub guarantees a replacement if someone cancels.

turns.speaker: Alice
turns.text: Let's work with SpeakerHub for the keynote, I'll brief them on the topics and the audience.

turns.speaker: Emma
turns.text: Who is our contact at SpeakerHub?

turns.speaker: Alice
turns.text: Our contact at SpeakerHub is Elena Rossi, she is the talent manager and she matches speakers to events.

turns.speaker: Emma
turns.text: Can I get her number to ask about the opening speaker's availability?

turns.speaker: Alice
turns.text: Yes, you can reach Elena Rossi at +33 6 12 34 56 07, she has a shortlist ready for us.

turns.speaker: Alice
turns.text: I'll review the shortlist with the team tomorrow so we pick the opening speaker together.

turns.speaker: Emma
turns.text: Picking together is a good idea, the opening talk really sets the tone for the whole day.

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: I'll take security and logistics, with three hundred people we need a proper plan for access and crowd flow.

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: We need badge checks at the entrance, clear emergency exits, and a few staff guiding people between rooms.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: We should also protect the equipment, the AV gear is expensive and it will be left in the room overnight.

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: Right, I'll arrange overnight coverage and a locked storage area for the valuable equipment.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: When do we need the security plan and staff in place?

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: The security plan must be finalized by April 8, and the staff need a briefing the day before the event.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: What budget is allocated to security?

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: The security budget is four thousand five hundred euros, covering the guards and the overnight coverage.

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: SafeGuard is the provider I trust, they do event security regularly and their staff are well trained.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: There is also SecureEvent, they are cheaper but I recall they were understaffed at a previous event.

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: SecureEvent being understaffed is exactly the risk we cannot take with three hundred guests, so I'll avoid them.

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: Let's hire SafeGuard for security, I'll send them the floor plan and the access requirements.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Who is our contact at SafeGuard?

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: Our contact at SafeGuard is Marc Dubois, he is the operations manager and he plans the staff deployment.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Can you share his number so I can coordinate the equipment storage?

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: Of course, you can reach Marc Dubois at +33 6 12 34 56 08, he will walk the venue with us.

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: I'll write a one-page security briefing so every staff member knows their role on the day.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: A clear one-pager is exactly what we need, thanks Bruno.

turns.speaker: Claire
turns.text: I'll handle press and media, getting coverage in the right outlets will amplify the launch well beyond the room.

turns.speaker: Claire
turns.text: We need a press kit with the product story, high-resolution images, and a clear embargo date for the announcements.

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: Make sure the embargo is respected, if the news leaks early it steals the thunder from the live keynote.

turns.speaker: Claire
turns.text: Absolutely, I'll set the embargo to the morning of May 20 and confirm it in writing with every journalist.

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: When do we need the press kit ready and the invitations sent?

turns.speaker: Claire
turns.text: The press kit has to be ready by April 12, so journalists have time to prepare their coverage before the event.

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: What budget do we have for press and media?

turns.speaker: Claire
turns.text: The press budget is two thousand five hundred euros, mostly for the kit design and a small media lunch.

turns.speaker: Claire
turns.text: MediaWave is my preferred partner, they have strong relationships with the tech journalists we want to reach.

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: Could we just email journalists ourselves? It saves money but we might miss the right contacts.

turns.speaker: Claire
turns.text: Doing it ourselves saves money but MediaWave's relationships get us coverage we could not reach alone, so it is worth it.

turns.speaker: Claire
turns.text: Let's work with MediaWave for press, I'll share the product story and the embargo details with them.

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: Who is our contact at MediaWave?

turns.speaker: Claire
turns.text: Our contact at MediaWave is Laura Chen, she is the media relations lead and she knows all the key journalists.

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: Can I get her number to coordinate the media lunch?

turns.speaker: Claire
turns.text: Yes, you can reach Laura Chen at +33 6 12 34 56 09, she is already drafting the invitation list.

turns.speaker: Claire
turns.text: I'll prepare the press kit this month so we are not rushing the images and the product story at the last minute.

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: Having the kit ready early is the right call, thanks Claire.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: I'll handle the merchandise, good quality swag leaves a lasting impression and people keep it for years.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: We want branded t-shirts, notebooks, and a reusable bottle, all in sizes and quantities for three hundred people.

turns.speaker: Hugo
turns.text: Please make the merchandise sustainable, cheap plastic giveaways would contradict the message of the product.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Totally, I'll choose organic cotton and recycled materials, and avoid single-use plastic entirely.

turns.speaker: Hugo
turns.text: When do we need to order the merchandise so it arrives on time?

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: We have to place the merchandise order by April 15, because production and shipping take about three weeks.

turns.speaker: Hugo
turns.text: What budget do we have for the merchandise?

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: The merchandise budget is three thousand five hundred euros, which is about eleven euros per person.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: PrintWorks is my recommendation, they do high-quality sustainable printing and they delivered well last time.

turns.speaker: Hugo
turns.text: There is also SwagCheap, the name says it all, but the quality reviews are pretty poor.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: SwagCheap is cheap but the poor quality would reflect badly on the brand, so I'd rather pay a little more.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Let's order from PrintWorks for the merchandise, I'll send them the designs and the size breakdown.

turns.speaker: Hugo
turns.text: Who is our contact at PrintWorks?

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Our contact at PrintWorks is Tom Weber, he is the production manager and he tracks every order.

turns.speaker: Hugo
turns.text: Can you share his number so I can confirm the delivery address?

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Sure, you can reach Tom Weber at +33 6 12 34 56 10, he will confirm the shipping timeline.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: I'll request a physical sample before the full run so we can check the quality with our own eyes.

turns.speaker: Hugo
turns.text: Checking a sample first is smart, thanks for keeping the quality bar high David.

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: Alright, we've covered all ten workstreams. Let's do a quick recap so everyone leaves knowing exactly what they own.

turns.speaker: Alice
turns.text: I own the venue with GrandHall and the keynote with SpeakerHub, both need to be locked by mid to late March.

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: I have catering with FreshTable and security with SafeGuard, with deadlines on March 20 and April 8.

turns.speaker: Claire
turns.text: I'm on the website with WebNova and press with MediaWave, live by April 2 and the kit ready by April 12.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: I handle audio and video with SoundPro and merchandise with PrintWorks, confirmed by March 28 and ordered by April 15.

turns.speaker: Emma
turns.text: I own registration with TicketFlow, opening by April 10, and I'll connect it to Claire's website.

turns.speaker: Hugo
turns.text: And I'm on sponsorship with BrandLink, targeting twenty thousand euros and signed by April 5.

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: Perfect. David will keep the shared checklist and the contact sheet, and we'll regroup here next week to check progress.

turns.speaker: Alice
turns.text: Thanks everyone, this was a productive meeting, let's keep all updates in this chat so nothing slips.

turns.speaker: Bruno
turns.text: Agreed, great work today, let's make the Aurora launch a real success.
